players.product: Layerscape control-plane processors for top-of-rack switches and SmartNICs

quarterly_data.signal: Record Q2 revenue was $3.5 billion, up 19% year-over-year and 10% sequentially; non-GAAP gross margin was 58%, operating margin 35.1%, EPS $3.61, and free cash flow $791 million or about 23% of revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: $3.5B revenue (+19% YoY, +10% QoQ); 35.1% operating margin; $3.61 EPS

quarterly_data.signal: NXP expects AI data-center revenue to rise from approximately $200 million in 2025 to more than $500 million in 2026. Its position is in the control plane: Layerscape processors are ramping from top-of-rack switching through SmartNIC control at leading hyperscalers, while NXP devices also control, monitor, cool and secure rack components.

Physical-AI adoption is already material: AI-enabled processors are expected to be about 15% of 2026 industrial and IoT processor revenue, more than double last year. The Kinara-based physical-AI design funnel expanded from more than $1 billion last quarter to more than $1.5 billion across over 200 distinct customers.
quarterly_data.figure: AI-enabled processors ~15% of 2026 industrial/IoT processor revenue; >$1.5B funnel across 200+ customers

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 guidance is revenue of $3.75 billion plus or minus $100 million, up 18% year-over-year and 7% sequentially, with non-GAAP gross margin of 58.5% plus or minus 50 basis points, operating margin of 36.9% and EPS of $4.11 at the midpoint.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 revenue $3.75B +/-$100M; GM 58.5% +/-50bps; operating margin 36.9%; EPS $4.11

quarterly_data.signal: Demand visibility improved into Q4 and Q1: backlog is growing across quarter-plus-one through quarter-plus-three, providing an 18-month signal; book-to-bill is above 1 and above last quarter, customer escalations doubled sequentially, and lead times above 16 weeks now cover a large part of the portfolio.
quarterly_data.figure: book-to-bill >1; 18-month backlog signal; escalations doubled QoQ; broad lead times >16 weeks

quarterly_data.signal: The next product wave is not yet in revenue: NXP's S32N 5-nanometer processor and S32K5 16-nanometer zonal-controller products remain in the design-win phase, while management said physical-AI deployments have not begun in earnest. Their future ramps underpin management's constructive 2027 outlook.
quarterly_data.figure: S32N 5nm and S32K5 16nm not yet ramping; physical-AI deployments still early
